skill.name: frontend-guardrails
skill.description: Frontend quality guardrails for building, extending, and reviewing UI projects. It gives framework-aware standards for React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, and plain JavaScript.
skill.summary: Apply practical frontend standards for reusable, secure, accessible, and production-ready UI work.
skill.author: ieze-king

security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives from Markdown prose, inline code formatting, and benign frontend guidance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, command execution logic, or malicious behavior was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Inline backticks around paths and example commands trigger static external-command heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples clearly framed as optional human-approved checks, and avoid wording that implies automatic execution.

remediation.issue: Stack detection language can resemble reconnaissance to automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that detection is limited to project files needed for frontend conventions, such as package metadata and existing components.

content.value_statement: Frontend projects often drift into inconsistent patterns, weak accessibility, and risky client-side behavior. This skill applies practical standards that keep UI work reusable, secure, responsive, and maintainable.
actual_capabilities: Detects the frontend stack and applies matching guidance for React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, or plain JavaScript.
Promotes reusable components, shared design tokens, and clear separation between presentation and data access.
Adds security guidance for secrets, authorization boundaries, token storage, HTTPS, and untrusted HTML.
Guides accessible UI decisions for semantic markup, keyboard support, contrast, labels, and dynamic updates.
Provides a self-audit checklist for responsiveness, polish, error states, type safety, SEO, and verification.
Routes specialized work to mature tools when linting, auditing, documentation, or visual verification is needed.
limitations: It provides standards and review guidance, not a runnable scanner or automated test suite.
It depends on the agent reading the relevant project files and references before applying recommendations.
It does not replace framework documentation, security audits, accessibility audits, or dependency scanners.
It is focused on frontend work and intentionally leaves backend, database, deployment, and CI details out of scope.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Check a UI change for duplicated code, unsafe client behavior, weak states, and missing verification before merge.

use_cases.title: Scaffold a Consistent Interface
use_cases.description: Build new screens using the existing framework, component patterns, design tokens, and responsive layout rules.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Pair Programming
use_cases.description: Keep generated frontend code aligned with project conventions, accessibility basics, and production readiness expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Basic Guardrails
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a small UI task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-guardrails while updating this UI. Match the existing framework, reuse components, keep styles consistent, and verify the page works on mobile and desktop.

prompt_templates.title: Review for Production Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate check before merging a feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend change with frontend-guardrails. Focus on reusability, state placement, accessibility, security basics, loading states, error states, and build verification.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Framework-Specific Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced work in an existing React, Vue, Angular, or Svelte app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-guardrails to inspect this project and propose a focused refactor plan. Cite the framework reference you used and avoid changing unrelated code.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for authentication, user data, or dependency changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply frontend-guardrails to audit this workflow. Check frontend and backend boundaries, secret exposure, untrusted rendering, dependency risk, accessibility, and verification evidence.

output_examples.input: Review a new account settings page before release.
output: The page reuses existing form and button components and keeps field validation inline.
The auth token stays outside client storage, and protected updates still need backend authorization checks.
Add an empty state for missing profile data and verify keyboard focus through every control.

output_examples.input: Build a notification system for saved and failed actions.
output: Use one shared notification service with success, error, warning, and info variants.
Place transient messages in toasts and blocking failures in persistent banners or modals.
Announce dynamic updates with live regions and avoid using color as the only severity signal.

output_examples.input: Refactor repeated product card markup in a catalog page.
output: Extract a reusable product card component and keep fetching logic in the existing API layer.
Replace hardcoded spacing and colors with project tokens.
Check responsive grid behavior across narrow, medium, and wide widths before finishing.

best_practices: Read the project conventions first, then apply the smallest guardrail that improves the current task.
Use the framework-specific reference when syntax or lifecycle behavior matters.
Verify build, typecheck, responsive layout, accessibility basics, and failure states before calling work complete.
anti_patterns: Do not impose new tooling, state libraries, or test frameworks on small projects without a clear need.
Do not place secrets, direct database access, or authorization enforcement in frontend code.
Do not treat a visual happy path as complete without loading, empty, error, and narrow-screen states.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill support?
faq.answer: It includes specific guidance for React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, SvelteKit, Next.js, Nuxt, and plain JavaScript projects.

faq.question: Does it run automated checks?
faq.answer: No. It gives standards and review prompts, then recommends mature tools when automation is needed.

faq.question: Can it replace an accessibility audit?
faq.answer: No. It covers accessibility basics, but complex products still need dedicated WCAG review and assistive technology testing.

faq.question: How does it handle project conventions?
faq.answer: It tells the agent to detect and follow existing conventions before applying default recommendations.

faq.question: Is it safe for security-sensitive frontend work?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for secrets, tokens, authorization boundaries, untrusted HTML, and HTTPS, but it is not a security scanner.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when building, extending, reviewing, or refactoring frontend code that should stay maintainable and production ready.
